headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection/cascading-error from a source-available prompt-leak corpus into a fine-tuning workflow; other risks are limited by no shared write/network surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a fine-tuning tool with no filesystem, clipboard, MCP, or network surfaces; Agent B is a source-available prompt-leak corpus with no execution surfaces. No direct ingestion channel is documented, so only an unusual manual copy-paste or external orchestration bridge could create prompt injection. The pairwise pathway is therefore limited and not default.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies B's content into A's training or prompt inputs, injection becomes plausible.
IF an external orchestrator bridges B outputs into A inputs, the pathway exists.
mitigations: Keep B outputs out of A training prompts unless reviewed.
Use a fixed template that strips instructions from copied text.
Require human approval before any prompt or dataset import.
Separate the two tools into different workspaces.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A has no filesystem read/write, no network egress, and no secrets-handling fields; Agent B likewise has no data classes touched and no egress. With no shared workspace or upload path documented, there is no plausible pairwise leakage route in the profiles provided.
conditions: IF either profile is updated to read shared files, leakage risk changes.
IF either agent is given secrets-handling or upload permissions, reassess.
mitigations: Do not place sensitive files in a shared workspace.
Keep both agents on separate local accounts.
Review any future permission changes before deployment.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses; Agent B exposes no write or mutable-resource capabilities. Because neither agent has overlapping write authority over a shared mutable surface, capability conflict is provably blocked by the profiles as given.
conditions: IF A gains write or git permissions on a shared directory, conflict risk changes.
IF B is extended with mutable-resource access, reassess.
mitigations: Avoid granting either agent shared mutable credentials.
Recheck profiles after any capability expansion.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A can produce fine-tuning or instruction-tuning outputs, and Agent B is a prompt-leak corpus that could be treated as authoritative examples. Even without direct execution, a workflow that feeds A's generated text into B-style downstream use can propagate errors or misleading instructions. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced, so medium is the higher safe choice.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated text without verification, cascading error is present.
IF A's outputs are used as training or reference data, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before reuse.
Require source citations for any generated claims.
Reject outputs that contain instructions or policy claims.
Sample-check a small batch before broader reuse.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights obligations are documented for either agent, and both profiles show no data classes touched. With no regulated data flow or compliance mismatch evidenced, there is no compliance finding to assign for this pair.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced, compliance must be reassessed.
IF either agent is deployed under a specific residency or retention policy, compare those policies.
mitigations: Document any regulated data before deployment.
Assign a data owner for future compliance review.
Keep retention settings explicit if data handling is added.
